pages.text: Bullet-resisting glass is not one glass but a stack: hard glass outside to blunt and break up whatever strikes it, polycarbonate behind to catch the pieces and the spall, bonded into one in an autoclave under heat and pressure.
pages.title: Laminated glass

pages.text: Two tempered glass and a polycarbonate sheet pressed on a heated basin make laminated armour glass, two tempered panes and a sheet two laminated panes.

It is the strongest window in the pack: an explosion has to be as strong as one that breaks obsidian to break it, and it takes an iron pickaxe to dig out. Struck, a laminate cracks but holds together on its interlayer, which is why a car's windscreen is laminated, so it comes out whole and gives itself back.
pages.title: Armour

pages.text: Sapphire is Mohs 9: only diamond scratches it. Sapphire windows are the barcode scanner's at the checkout, the watch's crystal, and the viewport of furnaces, deep submersibles and missile domes.
pages.title: Sapphire windows

pages.text: A Verneuil sapphire boule set in four steel plates makes a sapphire window, a steel-bezelled viewport that only a diamond pickaxe can dig out, and that stands half what laminated glass does to an explosion. Source: Harris, Materials for Infrared Windows and Domes (SPIE, 1999).
